newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool outlook remains optimistic.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool outlook remains optimistic.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue their gradual upward trend that began at the start of this season, pastrol group Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
"This week the market is expected to continue to be firm with the posibiltiy of price rises", Wesfarmers said.

Wesfarmers said there were a number of positive factors for the immediate market outlook. Japanese demand is expected to continue and, as this week's offering includes some better style Newcastle and Goulburn wools, finer micron prices are likely to rise further, it said. Also, the offerings over the next two weeks are small which will cause competition for quality types.
The eastern market indicator rose two cents to 614/kg clean.
The western market indicator rose seven cents to 556/kg clean, after a two week break.
Following a meeting in Melbourne last week, wool industry sectors reached a consensus regarding changes to stockpile disposal arrangements, Wesfarmers Dalgety noted.
The majority agreed to recommend that the legislation governing stockpile disposal be modified to allow the sale of a minimum of 90,000 and a maximum of 250,000 bales per quarter.
